design_rationale: The study explicitly states that participants were randomly allocated using block randomization across two centres into three study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: While block randomization was used, allocation concealment methods are not reported, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prospective randomization of the patients was carried out using block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions were intraoperative surgical products delivered according to protocol, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All of the 996 patients investigated, 332 patients (33.3%) were prospectively randomized into the S-group, whereas 336 patients (33.7%) were randomized into the G-group and 328 patients (32.9%) into the I-group... All of the 996 patients were analysed

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available and analyzed for all 996 randomized participants with no reported loss to follow-up for the primary end-point.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All of the 996 patients were analysed concerning preoperative data... intraoperative data... perioperative data... and postoperative data (sternum stability, superficial and deep SSI of the sternum).

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper does not state whether outcome assessors were blinded to treatment group assignment when diagnosing surgical site infection, introducing some concerns of detection bias for this partially subjective clinical outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: According to the Centers for Disease Control, SSIs are grouped into superficial and deep SSI [10]. Superficial sternal SSI is limited to the skin and subcutaneous tissue, whereas deep sternal SSI involves muscle, fascia, sternum and organ/spaces.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or pre-published statistical analysis protocol is cited, leaving some concerns regarding potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary study end-point was to analyse the incidence of superficial and deep sternal SSI in patients following isolated CABG with median sternotomy in the three different groups (S-group, G-group and I-group) during hospital stay and after 3 months postoperatively.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of details regarding allocation concealment, absence of blinding of surgical site infection outcome assessors, and lack of a cited pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study is a randomized controlled trial where an external statistician generated the allocation sequence using computer generation with variable block sizes and allocation was concealed in sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with variable block sizes, concealed in sealed envelopes opened only at wound closure, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An external statistician who was not involved in the enrolment or assessment of the patients performed the randomization. The allocation sequence was computergenerated with a variable block size of 8, 12, or 16 patients and was stratified for center. Assignments were concealed in sealed envelopes. At the end of the operation, immediately before sternal closure, the envelope was opened and the patient was allocated to a treatment group... or a control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and postoperative care providers/assessors were blinded to assignment, no substantial deviations from the intended protocol were reported, and analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was randomized, prospective, and doubleblind (ie, the patients and those physicians and nurses who collected all the postoperative data and classified the infections were blinded regarding what treatment the patients had received)... No documentation concerning the group to which the patient had been randomized was left in the patient’s file.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for over 99% of randomized participants with only 6 of 1956 patients lost to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, 1956 patients entered the study. Six of these could not be reached at the follow-up... Evaluation was possible in 967 and 983 patients in the control and treatment groups, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome of sternal wound infection was assessed using standardized CDC criteria by assessors and a senior surgeon who were blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was randomized, prospective, and doubleblind (ie, the patients and those physicians and nurses who collected all the postoperative data and classified the infections were blinded regarding what treatment the patients had received)... All classifications were made by the same person, a senior surgeon (Ö.F.), before the randomization code was broken.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint was predefined and reported in full, with analysis according to an intention-to-treat framework without indications of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end-point was any SWI within 2 months postoperatively... Subgroup analyses with regard to bacterial etiology, depth of infection and established preoperative risk groups (diabetes and high body mass index [BMI]) were conducted.

overall_summary: The trial was rigorously conducted with computer-generated central randomization, sealed envelope concealment, blinded outcome assessors and participants, minimal loss to follow-up (<1%), and predefined outcome reporting, resulting in a low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, randomized controlled trial where patients were randomized to either the gentamicin-collagen implant group or the control group using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although sealed envelopes were used, there is no information about sequence generation or whether the envelopes were sequentially numbered and opaque, and consent was only asked from the intervention group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomized to the gentamicin group or the control group using sealed envelopes. In the study group, the subjects gave their informed consent. The controls were not asked for informed consent because no additional appointments or investigations were necessary.

domain_judgments.rationale: The surgical intervention took place under general anesthesia, standard co-interventions were balanced between groups, and all randomized patients were analyzed in their allocated groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients in the gentamicin group received a 10 cm!10 cm gentamicin-collagen implant (Gentacoll, Schering-Plough, PO 3, 02201 Espoo, Finland)... underneath their sternum before wound closure... The controls’ sternums were closed in a routine manner with steel wires, without a gentamicin implant.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for sternal wound infection were reported for all 542 randomized patients with complete 3-month follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were followed-up three months after discharge from hospital... Postoperative sternal wound infections occurred in 11 of 272 patients (4.0%) in the study group and in 16 of 270 patients (5.9%) in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated CDC criteria were used and the diagnosing assessors were blinded to the study group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Assessment of surgicalsite infections (SSIs) was made according to the criteria published by the Centers for Disease Control in 1992... The diagnosis of sternum infection was made either by a cardiac surgeon or an infection consultant who was not involved in this study and who did not know which study group each patient belonged to.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-published protocol is referenced to verify that the reported analyses and outcomes were pre-specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The aim of this study was to show the possible effects of local gentamicin in the prevention of sternal wound infections in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns regarding the randomization process (unclear sequence generation and concealment details, with consent requested only post-randomization in the intervention arm) and potential selection of the reported result in the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospectively randomized, double-blind trial where 800 patients were assigned to receive either a gentamicin-collagen sponge or a pure collagen sponge (placebo).

domain_judgments.rationale: Central randomization was performed by an independent clinical trials center with allocation concealment maintained via numbered identical sponges, and baseline differences are minimal and consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization and blinding were carried out by the Centre for Clinical Studies of Würzburg University Hospital. After randomization, the 400 gentamicin-collagen sponges and the 400 placebo sponges were labeled with a sticker showing the randomization number.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the intervention was double-blind with identical sponges, 80 randomized patients (10%) were excluded post-randomization (including non-use of the sponge, perioperative mortality, and revision for bleeding), meaning analysis was not an intention-to-treat analysis and post-randomization exclusions could introduce bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 720 of 800 (90%) of the screened patients were included in the study analysis after the end of the 30-day follow-up period after index surgery. Some 80 of 800 patients (10%) could not be evaluated, the reasons being revision surgery because of bleeding (40x), perioperative mortality not associated with a wound infection (20x), and non-use of the specified sponge (20x).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing/excluded for 10% of randomized participants (80/800) due to revision, early mortality, or non-use, and the breakdown of these missing cases per study arm is not fully detailed or analyzed under intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Some 80 of 800 patients (10%) could not be evaluated, the reasons being revision surgery because of bleeding (40x), perioperative mortality not associated with a wound infection (20x), and non-use of the specified sponge (20x).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and patients were blinded with identical placebos, and objective, standardized CDC diagnostic criteria with microbiological verification were used to assess sternal wound infections.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 2 sponges looked identical and could not be differentiated by the surgeon on the basis of their appearance or haptic characteristics... DSWI and SSWI were defined on the basis of the criteria of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention as a positive bacterial culture from mediastinal tissue or fluid, and an intraoperative clinical picture of mediastinitis...

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (ISRCTN 20849) and the primary and secondary outcomes were reported according to a pre-specified analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered at Current Controlled Trials Limited, London with the assign ISRCTN 20849... The primary end point of the study was the occurrence of a DSWI/mediastinitis within the 30-day follow-up period after index surgery.

overall_summary: The study is generally well-conducted and blinded, but some concerns arise in Domains 2 and 3 due to the post-randomization exclusion of 80 randomized patients (10%) without a clear intention-to-treat analysis. Consequently, the overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective randomized controlled trial where participants were allocated using a central interactive voice response system with stratified random block sizes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation was random with block sizes, allocation was concealed via a central IVRS after incision, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization occurred after surgical incision using a central randomization interactive voice response system, thus providing complete allocation concealment. The randomization scheme was stratified by site and random block sizes were used.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients remained blinded, standard surgical and antibiotic protocols were strictly mandated across both arms without important protocol deviations affecting the outcome, and analysis followed intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To avoid possible bacterial growth on an unimpregnated sponge, patients in the control group did not receive a placebo sponge. As a result, surgeons were not blinded to study group assignment... Standard care was standardized including prophylactic systemic antibiotics and rigid sternal fixation... The primary study comparison was done in the intent-to-treat population.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were nearly complete, with only 12 out of 1502 randomized participants (0.8%) lacking information on the primary outcome, balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of note, only 31 individuals (2.1%) were lost to follow-up at 90 days (13 in the gentamicin-collagen sponge group and 18 in the control group). Only 12 of 1502 individuals did not contribute information to the primary end point.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment was conducted by an independent clinical events classification committee blinded to treatment assignment using standard CDC and ASEPSIS criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The independent clinical events classification committee was composed of 3 infectious disease experts blinded to the treatment assignments... clinical events classification committee determined the presence or absence, extent, and severity of all possible infections using standardized criteria including those from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the ASEPSIS scoring system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT00600483), had a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and reported primary and secondary outcomes consistent with prespecified plans.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial Registration clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT00600483... The primary study outcome was the incidence of sternal wound infection occurring within the period from surgery through postoperative day 90... The per-protocol population, as defined in the statistical analysis plan, included all randomized patients who completed the study and had none of the following prespecified major protocol deviations

overall_summary: The trial was methodologically rigorous with centralized random allocation, blinded outcome adjudication by an independent committee, virtually complete follow-up, and prespecified intention-to-treat analyses, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.
